title: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
description: == performs type coercion before comparison, while === checks both value and type without coercion.

data.text: **Question:** What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
== performs type coercion before comparison, while === checks both value and type without coercion. Always prefer === for predictable comparisons.

**== (Loose Equality):
- Performs type coercion before comparing
- Can lead to unexpected results
- 0 == false returns true
- '' == false returns true

**=== (Strict Equality):
- Checks both value and type
- No type coercion
- 0 === false returns false
- '' === false returns false

**Best Practice:**
- Always use === unless you explicitly need coercion
- Makes code more predictable
- Easier to debug
